extracted.intended_audience: American short-story authors, magazine contributors, editors, and readers (writers seeking publication and those consulting yearbook selections)
extracted.subtask_description: Contains publication-address guidance for authors and the Yearbook's selection/notation rules for the Biographical Roll of Honor (which lists and annotates notable American short stories for 1917).

rubrics_metrics.name: Address list scope / completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Note. This address list does not aim to be complete, but is based simply on the magazines which I have considered for this volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that the list of magazine addresses that follows is selective (not exhaustive) and reflects only the magazines the editor considered when preparing this yearbook; users should treat it as a practical, limited submission resource rather than a comprehensive directory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magazines publishing short stories (addresses)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of magazines and their mailing addresses (e.g., Ainslee's Magazine, All-Story Weekly, Atlantic Monthly, Collier's Weekly, Cosmopolitan, Harper's Magazine, Scribner's Magazine, Saturday Evening Post, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a practical resource for authors seeking markets for short stories; includes many prominent U.S. magazines of the period with street addresses for submissions. Because the list is selective (see scope note), authors should verify current submission policies and consider additional markets beyond those listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roll of Honor: nationality restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Note. Only stories by American authors are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Biographical Roll of Honor and its selections are explicitly limited to American authors; non-American authors and their stories are therefore excluded from this particular roll and its 'best' designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best sixty-three stories indicated
rubrics_metrics.description: The best sixty-three stories are indicated by an asterisk before the title of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starred items identify the editor's top selections (the 'best' sixty-three). The asterisk is the presentation/selection marker used in the Roll of Honor to distinguish standout stories from the broader list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for prior Roll inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The index figures I, 2, and 3 prefixed to the name of the author indicate that his work has been included in the Rolls of Honor for 1914, 1915, and 1916 respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides provenance metadata: prefixed numerals show which authors were previously honored in past Rolls of Honor (I = 1914, 2 = 1915, 3 = 1916). Useful for readers tracking recurring recognition and for signaling sustained quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Roll entry contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Author entries include brief biographical details (birthplace and year), education, early publishing history, principal works, residence, occupations/interests, and a list of stories (with starred 'best' titles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Roll entry combines personal and bibliographic information to contextualize the author's work and to justify inclusion. For editors/compilers, this indicates the expected elements when presenting honored authors: concise biography, career highlights, and annotated list of stories.
